text:
oliver: Quick heads-up — post-canary in us-east-1 for the quantized path showed steady RSS creep and 2 OOMs around 03:20 UTC. Canaries running 4.2.1-rc with quant path enabled.

oliver: Short paste of the OOM-ish log we got (trimmed):
```text
[2026-03-17T03:19:58Z] runtime.ERROR: OutOfMemory: allocation failed after 1048576 bytes
  at decode_loop() +0x3f2
  at kv_cache::store() +0x9b
  ...
```

oliver: Key observables: baseline pod RSS ~1.3GB -> ~1.9GB over ~3h. Token throughput steady, CPU not spiking. KV-cache hit rate in metrics looks normal.

anya: :eyes: can you paste the exact commit and canary IDs? I can pull heapshots once the pods are up.

oliver: commit d4b2f7e (service/runtime: quant path tweak). Canary IDs: canary-128, canary-129. Runtime flags: --kv-cache=enabled --kv-ttl=30m --smallalloc-threshold=256

kevin: I can run jemalloc stats + flamegraph on a repro. Please drop a tiny repro loop I can run against a staging canary.

oliver: repro loop (python):
```python
import requests
for i in range(2000):
    r = requests.post('https://canary-us-east.redwood/api/v1/generate', json={'prompt':'test '*50, 'max_tokens':32})
    if i % 100 == 0:
        print(i, r.status_code)
```

sophia: FYI PR #4123 touched the arena allocation path for quantized models — pinging @kevin and @maria. Could be a subtle fragmentation/arena growth thing.

maria: I'm on it. I'll run the smallalloc microbench on the same image and dump heap snapshots at ~1h and ~3h. Preferred tooling? pprof or jemalloc jeprof?

kevin: jemalloc + jeprof snapshots are useful here. Also capture MALLOC_CONF and je_malloc_stats_print output. I'll prepare a sidecar to collect those automatically.

perf-bot: (auto) benchmark summary: canary-quantized-4.2.1-rc — 3h mem trend +25% avg, allocation churn concentrated in decode path. Link: https://perf.redwood/bench/1832

deploy-bot: rolling redeploy: canary image -> 4.2.1-rc+jeprof (adds jemalloc hooks). New pods expected in ~4m.

anya: I'll collect heapshots once the replaced canaries are stable. @oliver can you tag the failing request IDs and attach any request-specific inputs?

oliver: tagged failing requests in the incident note, and left two sample payloads in /tmp/canary-repro.json. Also tried a local tweak: lowering --smallalloc-threshold to 128 reduced RSS by ~60MB in a local loop (not a full test). Won't push without review.

sophia: good signal. @maria can you include the 128 threshold in the microbench matrix? If it consistently reduces RSS we can make it an experiment flag behind a runtime toggle.

maria: yep — including it. I'll run 128/256/512 and capture fragmentation metrics (arena sizes, retained pages). Assigning myself to follow up and open a task on the eng-runtime board.

kevin: quick diagnostic tip: if resident increases without corresponding heap allocs, check for kernel page retention from mmap/madvise (look at /proc/<pid>/smaps and anon hugepages). I'll run pmap + smem on the canary pods when they're up.

oliver: thanks all. If anyone reproduces or sees similar memory creep, post findings here. Otherwise I'll wait for the heapshots from @anya and the microbench results from @maria. :thumbsup:
